idiom_name: LazyList.iterate / LazyList.cons with memoized element computation
implementation_notes: LazyList is Scala's memoizing lazy collection: an immutable linked list that computes its elements only when needed and memoizes them, so the realized prefix is shared between traversals and an infinite definition is safe to hold as a value; LazyList.iterate/continually/from build unbounded sequences, and the standard combinators stay lazy. Choose it when elements are expensive and re-read; because the memoized prefix is never released, a long-lived LazyList over a huge source is a retention problem - use .view or Iterator for one-pass streaming, and replace the deprecated Stream (pre-2.13) with LazyList.
code_sketch:
val fib: LazyList[BigInt] =                 // memoized, potentially infinite
  LazyList.iterate((BigInt(0), BigInt(1))) { case (a, b) => (b, a + b) }.map(_._1)

val firstEven = fib.filter(_ % 2 == 0).take(10).toList   // forces ten, caches prefix
pitfalls: LazyList memoizes strongly: holding the head after traversing a huge prefix retains every realized element (the canonical lazy-list leak); release the head or use a non-caching view.
Deeply recursive lazy definitions (def fib: LazyList[...] = ... fib ...) can overflow the stack instead of looping, because each forced element nests a frame.
Traversing an infinite LazyList with a strict operation (length, max, sorting, groupBy) never terminates; every consumer must take a finite prefix.

variants.name: View-based collections (non-memoized views)
variants.implementation_notes: Scala's collections implement operations view-based: xs.view returns a lazy view that applies transforms per element on demand instead of building intermediate collections, so the same declarative pipeline runs without materializing stage outputs and works over very large or generated sources. Views are transient and not memoized - they recompute on every traversal and observe changes to the underlying collection - so they are the right choice for one-pass consumption, while LazyList is the right choice when elements must be cached, and an eager collection when the data is small or reused.
variants.code_sketch:
val evensSquared =
  (1 to 1000000).view.filter(_ % 2 == 0).map(n => n * n)   // lazy view

val first = evensSquared.take(5).toList                    // forces five elements
pitfalls: Views are not cached: iterating the same view twice recomputes everything, and a view over a mutable collection reflects later mutations (a surprise for callers expecting a snapshot).
View semantics changed across the 2.12/2.13 redesign (Stream deprecated, views non-caching), so code copied from older examples may assume the wrong laziness or caching behaviour.
Mixing strict and lazy operations (view.map(...).toList.sortBy(...)) silently materializes the whole source at the strict boundary; an infinite source must never reach it.
